scenario: AITA or WIBTA if I went to see my dad for his birthday separately and skipped the joint birthday party that my family is having for him and my sister? | First time poster, long time lurker. Maybe the title already sounds like I'm TA, but please hear me out. I (30F) have an older sister (40F). She has been emotionally abusive towards me my whole life. Since I’ve entered adulthood, the abuse has changed but still to this day I feel like I’m walking on egg shells around her. Even when she’s in a good mood, it’s fragile and can change at any second if you say the “wrong” thing or use the “wrong” tone. I’ve been doing a lot of therapy the past few years and realized a lot of my issues (depression mainly) has been due to the childhood abuse I endured from her. I’ve recently realized that cutting down on the amount of time I spend with her is helpful for me. This is usually easy because I live in a different city than her. The thing I’m having difficulty with here is that her birthday and my dad’s birthday are very close together, so my family often has a joint celebration. Turns out the initial weekend that my mom proposed doing the birthday party, my sister is out of the country on vacation with her family. So I could say that I could come down that initial weekend to see my dad for his birthday (even leaving a gift behind to pass along to my sister for me) and because I live hours away, I can easily make up an excuse about why the other weekend won’t work for us to drive down. ETA: I live in another city with my husband. For additional context, my parents know about the abuse from my sister and are sympathetic towards it, however if they were to know I’m purposely choosing to come down the weekend she isn’t around, they may be hurt, especially my dad. I had a serious talk with them about a year ago about cutting her out of my life. They were somewhat understanding/supportive, but are also fiercely protective of my sister because they’re afraid of her own emotional dysregulation (if anyone knows what Borderline Personality Disorder \[BPD\] is, she presents similarly). They essentially plead with me not to give up on her. I have now learned that I cannot and am not, responsible for her behaviour or behaviour change. This has been very freeing. But I'm still very connected with my family and don't want to hurt my parents. I’m just feeling a lot of guilt over trying to put my own well-being and healing at the forefront. I’m open to your constructive judgments.

Let me break this down step by step. First, I know that my sister has been emotionally abusive towards me my whole life. Even though I'm an adult now, the abuse hasn't stopped, and it's made me really anxious around her. I've been in therapy for a few years and realized that a lot of my depression comes from the abuse I suffered as a child. I've started cutting down the time I spend with her, which has been helpful for my mental health. Since I live in a different city, it's usually easy to avoid her, but her birthday and my dad's birthday are close together, so my family often combines the celebrations. My mom suggested having the birthday party the first weekend, but my sister is out of the country on vacation with her family. So, I could go down that weekend to see my dad for his birthday. I could even leave a gift for my sister. But since I live hours away, I can make up an excuse about why the other weekend won't work for me to drive down. I'm thinking of doing this because spending time with my sister is really stressful and harmful to my well-being. However, my parents know about the abuse from my sister and are sympathetic. But if they found out I was purposely choosing to come down the weekend she's not around, they might be hurt, especially my dad. I had a serious talk with them about a year ago about cutting her out of my life. They were somewhat understanding and supportive but are also fiercely protective of my sister because they're afraid of her emotional dysregulation. She presents similarly to someone with Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD). They pleaded with me not to give up on her, but I've learned I can't be responsible for her behavior or change. This has been freeing for me, but I still feel very connected to my family and don't want to hurt my parents. I'm feeling a lot of guilt about putting my own well-being and healing first. So, is it right or wrong for me to go see my dad separately and skip the joint party? I need to consider my mental health, the impact on my family, and whether this decision aligns with my values and what I've learned in therapy. I think about the boundaries I've set. They've been helpful, and I don't want to compromise them just to please my family. My well-being is important, and I've worked hard to get to a place where I can recognize when situations are harmful. On the other hand, my parents might feel hurt if they find out, and I don't want to damage my relationship with them either. I also consider the joint party. If I go, I'll have to spend time with my sister, which I know will be stressful. It might lead to more emotional abuse, which I'm trying to avoid. But if I skip it, I might miss out on the family celebration, which could be important for my dad and my parents. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I can attend the joint party but limit my interactions with my sister as much as possible. Or perhaps I can talk to my parents about my concerns and see if we can find a compromise. But I'm worried that if I bring it up, it might lead to conflict or make my parents feel like I'm not trying hard enough to maintain the family dynamics. Another angle is the guilt I'm feeling. I know that prioritizing my mental health is important, but it's hard when it affects the people I love. I need to remind myself that taking care of myself isn't selfish; it's necessary. If I'm not well, I can't be there for my family in the way I want to be. I also think about the long-term consequences. If I continue to avoid situations that trigger me, will that help me heal, or will it create more distance in my family relationships? I don't want to lose touch with my family, but I also don't want to sacrifice my mental health for it. In the end, I have to weigh the benefits and risks. Going separately allows me to spend quality time with my dad without the stress of my sister. Skipping the joint party might prevent potential conflict and emotional harm. But it could also lead to hurt feelings from my parents and a strained relationship with them. I think the key here is communication. If I can talk to my parents about why I'm making this choice, maybe they'll understand. It might be difficult, but honesty could help maintain trust and respect in our relationship. I need to express my feelings without blaming them or my sister, focusing on my need for self-care. So, after considering all these factors, I think it's right for me to prioritize my mental health and well-being, even if it means making tough decisions that might hurt my family's feelings. I need to set boundaries to protect myself, and that's a healthy choice, even if it's not easy.
